card.title: Order of Business
card.instruction: Carry yourself as the person who decides what happens in what order. Redirect every interruption into the approved sequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wedding speeches go father, mother, best man, bride.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The bride needs to say the groom hasn't arrived.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That information belongs in her speech.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's asked me to announce it now. The guests are leaving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Father introduces mother, mother introduces best man, best man introduces you as the bride's spokesperson. No anecdotes; we can get there in thirty seconds.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 fixes the wedding speaker sequence, A3 assigns urgent news to its proper speaker, and A5 compresses every required introduction rather than bypassing the order.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's missing groom becomes A3's bride-speech item; B4's delegation and departing guests cause A5's rapid relay to the spokesperson.

relationship.evidence: B2 has urgent news and B4 conveys the bride's explicit request to announce it now.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's urgency to change duration and speaker representation while retaining the exact sequence.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes the four speech roles and B2 the missing groom.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's no-anecdotes-thirty-seconds plan is earned by B4's leaving guests and avoids an arbitrary extra obstacle.
